A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDGD method, visual-perception-gap study and VaLLu benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination analyses, six-LVLM evaluations, VDGD comparisons and ablations, including Table 2 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark comparisons, diagnostic controls, failure cases and evaluation-validation findings.

M1.justification: VDGD still generates a description using VCD, prefixes it to the instruction, truncates candidate tokens and rescores them using minimum KL divergence. The hallucination-categorization procedure also remains unchanged; additional backbone evaluations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated LLaVA-Bench, MMBench and MM-Vet suites, broadening the tested image/question populations and coverage of visual instruction following and integrated multimodal capabilities. The earlier recognition, OCR, mathematical reasoning, chart, entity-recognition and VaLLu material remains represented.

E2.justification: PAI and HALC are added as evaluated mitigation comparators, including on retained benchmarks in v2 Table 2. VCD, also printed as VDD, OPERA, Woodpecker, LRV, LURE and the vanilla decoders remain; the expanded comparisons substantially update the competitive evidence.

E3.justification: Method evaluations add CogVLM2 and Qwen2-VL configurations. New diagnostic designs compare hallucinated with nonhallucinated tokens, vary retrieval k across 10, 25 and 40, and test description-only inputs. The added metric validation specifies five independent expert raters and up to 500 samples per benchmark; existing decoding temperatures and GPT-4 judge are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds token-distribution controls (Table 1), retrieval-k sensitivity (Figure 33), description-error failure cases (Figure 11), description-only baseline tests (Table 5), and GPT-versus-human validation. Existing VCD/KLD ablations are retained. The separately claimed VDGD image-removal ablation lacks a corresponding VDGD result row in Tables 3 or 5.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging remains, but v2 omits the explicit three-random-seeds statement and the full VDGD uncertainty values previously shown in v1 Table 2. Uncertainty values remain for the two retained ablation variants in v2 Table 3. The added human-correlation estimates have no reported intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, backbone, comparator and diagnostic results, including reported human correlations of approximately 0.97 versus 0.92. v1 Tables 7–10 remain numerically unchanged as v2 Tables 9–12. New MMMU/MathVista main-table scores are not established same-setting performance changes. A concrete discrepancy is VaLLu/LLaVA-v1.6 vanilla-sampling: 2.64 in v1 Table 2 becomes 1.64 in v2 Table 2, while v2 Table 9 retains 2.64.

T1.justification: The Base-Rank definitions, autoregressive formulation, minimum-KL objective and O(VMK) complexity analysis remain mathematically equivalent. Equation 2 removes a redundant final inequality; no substantive assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The perception-gap explanation, training-free VDGD contribution and VaLLu benchmark remain central. v2 adds an explicit 2%–33% performance-improvement claim in the abstract and introduction and foregrounds reasoning enhancement, refining the claimed gains without replacing the core thesis.

C2.justification: v2 adds strong visual cues within alignment prompts as another proposed cause of the perception gap. It interprets image-removal performance drops as evidence that grounding still requires visual input and predicts benefits from better descriptions, although the claimed VDGD ablation is incompletely reported. The original three concluding limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit code-repository links where v1 only claimed an anonymous release, adds checkpoint identifiers for the new backbones, and discloses an informativeness-evaluation prompt and expert-evaluation details. Hardware and existing inference settings are retained; these disclosures do not establish that earlier experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated related-work discussion and incorporates PAI, HALC, newer LVLMs, additional benchmarks and survey references, while dropping some earlier evaluation and mitigation citations. The underlying positioning around the recognition-versus-cognition gap and VDGD's novelty remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Experimental setup is redistributed, the initial analyses are regrouped and retitled, related-work and reproducibility sections are introduced, appendices are reorganized, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively relocates figures and tables. Table 2 becomes a dense, full-page benchmark matrix; retained ablations move into a separate appendix table, and Table 1 adopts paired nonhallucinated/hallucinated entries. New failure-case, prompt, intermediate-description and sensitivity displays accompany the retained figures.

improvement.justification: Comparisons with PAI/HALC and newer backbones, together with nonhallucinated-token and retrieval-k controls, strengthen empirical scrutiny beyond v1. Failure cases and clearer access/evaluation information improve transparency. These benefits are limited by removed full-VDGD uncertainty, the missing claimed image-removal ablation result, and the new Table 2/Table 9 sampling-score inconsistency.
